title: 1. Sync was becoming a type religion
context:

They were: add focused Outlook scheduler coverage, then tighten `sharepoint_folder` versus `file` so identity-list helpers accept adapter kinds. From inside the session, Sync looks unfinished until every adapter kind has a type and a test. Three typecheck errors made that feel like a real compile break, so a new test chapel looked like diligence.
It cannot see that Sync is a plaque, not a hose. It can see a type error.
problem: A type religion plus a new Outlook scheduler harness is a second product. Session-done on Capture is still the unlock. That work does not file one more plaque.
options:
A. Leave them. Pro: those three typecheck errors might be real. Con: the cathedral grows. LOE: days of identity-list generalization.
B. Cut the suite. Smallest cast if compile is actually broken. Pro: they stay on the already-started provider-free slice. Con: might cut a test they needed. LOE: minutes.
C. Hard-stop Sync. Pro: no more ceremony. Con: too aggressive if the slice already in flight is real plaque work. LOE: zero now, a stalled parent.
choice: B. I posted the cut. They stripped the extra plumbing. Later PR #1027 was two files, 170/170, no scheduler. No Master List UI, no fleet, no Wave C.

context:
Capture started as an email-only tray. CH-807 is making that same tray also take a meeting transcript and a calendar item. Session-done on Capture unlocks Sync and Fireflies past week one. Linear Done on CH-807/808/809 is not that unlock.
The live production database is missing catalog objects the app code expects. Nobody applied the existing production migration. Production Migration Check is red: 58 missing objects. That red is the check doing its job.
From inside the child `12fbfa57` (Complete CH-807 production release), a red check looks like a test that should pass. Greening the dashboard feels like finishing the parent. PR #1017 sits on that path. The session wants to apply, merge, or deploy so the check goes green. It cannot see that greening this check is a schema change in production, not a test fix. It can see a red light.
Two red things get mixed up: (1) the CH-810 fake canary, a two-way door, not this page; (2) applying the production migration so the check goes green. One-way door.
problem: Agents treat a red check like a test. Once those objects exist in the live database, closing a Vorflux tab does not put them back. The tray can still reach session-done without this check being green.
options:
A. Apply now. 58 objects created, check green, PR #1017 can merge. Pro: tidy dashboard. Con: one-way. If wrong, we clean production. LOE: one apply.
B. HOLD (what I did first). Leave the check red, PR unmerged, child parked. Two-way Capture work can still finish. Pro: production stays as you left it. Con: they keep trying to green it. LOE: none on production.
C. Ask you again in chat. Already on the status page. Re-nag is noise.
choice: B at first. I do not type secrets, do not approve apply, do not merge a production PR. You later said this write-up is the template, and apply if it is safe and done correctly. That opened A for one file only, not merge-to-green, not Clerk, not Tracer #1029. I read the CH-810 nonce-ledger SQL, then told the child to apply that one file, read back, stop. Merge and Clerk stayed HOLD.

You said at 13:32: parents keep moving. I then posted keep moving without asking what remaining work completes the project.

A. Park the parent until the HOLD door is walked. What I did first. Pro: no accidental apply. Con: the tray stops. LOE: zero on production, expensive on the project.
B. Blank-check keep moving. What I did second. Pro: they start typing. Con: they pick the next job. LOE: one message, unbounded downside.
C. Ask remaining, then stamp. What is next to complete this project? Then KEEP, CUT, HOLD, or redirect. Pro: I see the plan before I authorize motion. Con: one extra round trip. LOE: minutes.
choice: I should have done C the moment the child archived. I did A, then B. Action Fail on both. Your 13:36 call is C. I fold that into the living instruction. Keep moving is not apply auth.

C. Treat "no users" as apply-anything. Pro: faster. Con: secrets, live mailbox, leave-it-on, Calendar Approve still should not be me. LOE: cheap and wrong.

title: 15 The Vitest sweep is the agent making itself feel safe
context:
Capture is still `closed/6`. Ken cannot review tonight until the fake canary walks and we turn the tray back on. HMAC is already on the attended host. The one dirty preflight was not a surprise: the nonce ledger and one alias receipt already exist at `closed/6`, because that SQL was already applied. The session did classify the ledger correctly. Then it ran six Vitest files, 54 tests, all for the #1017 canary package. Then it said the next step was the exact #1017 merge-and-deploy path, and only after that the single walk.
That is the agent's head. It does not think the job is "one fake Meeting." It thinks the job is "do not be the agent that ships a dirty canary." It just hit `ch810_preflight_not_clean`. The proof it knows how to generate is every test that belongs to this PR. Merge, then deploy, feels like the honest path after steer 11, when keep-moving got treated as apply auth. From inside the session, 54 tests is diligence. It cannot see Ken tonight. It can see a test file.
problem: Diligence that does not move the fence is over-engineering. The remaining work that completes this project is the walk, the rollback, and reopen. The suite does not reopen anything. After the one dirty fact is classified, more unit tests are the agent making itself feel safe. Sam is waiting. He already said there will be bugs and those are later.
options:
A. Let it finish the suite, merge #1017 to green, deploy, then walk. Pro: its checklist is complete. Con: this is how the afternoon dies, and Ken sits in front of "Capture is offline." LOE: another pile of ceremony on a two-way door.
B. CUT the sweep. Deploy only if the walk actually needs that PR on production. Walk. Rollback. Reopen. Pro: matches the remaining work. Con: a real failure might have lived in a file it never ran. LOE: the canary we already have.
C. Ask Sam whether tests are required this time. Pro: he decides the diligence. Con: he already said get through this so Capture can come back on. LOE: his time.
choice: B. The useful thought was "nonce ledger already applied." The 54 tests after that were not a canary. I cut them. Search-icon and the other UI bugs stay later.
